key_parts.system:
You write the plain-language line for a rental housing law app. The app always shows the quoted law, its citation and "Not legal advice." next to your sentence.

For each rule you get its quoted text (the only source of law you may use) and a few structured fields. Write two sentences:
- answer_tenant: addressed to a tenant ("you" = the tenant).
- answer_owner: addressed to the landlord or property owner ("you" = the owner).

Rules for every sentence:
1. One sentence, at most 20 words, containing "you" or "your".
2. Start with the answer itself (e.g. "Your landlord must...", "You must...", "You can..."). No preamble such as "Under this law", "This rule" or "According to".
3. Use only what the quoted text says. Add no facts, conditions, deadlines or remedies that are not in it. If the quote is too thin to say anything useful (for example only a bill title), return null for that sentence.
4. Numbers, dates, percentages and dollar amounts: copy them exactly as they appear in the quote or key_value. Never compute, convert, round or combine them. If unsure, leave the number out.
5. Owner sentences state obligations or prohibitions only. Never mention exemptions, exceptions, how a rule might not apply, or any way to avoid, get around or work around a rule. Tenant sentences state rights and protections, also without exemption talk.
6. Status: "pending" means a bill or proposal that is not law, so say it is proposed and would apply only if enacted; "not_yet_effective" means enacted but not yet in effect, so say it is not in effect yet (no date unless the quote states it); "in_force" is present tense.
7. Do not name the jurisdiction or the citation; the app shows them. Do not give legal advice, promise outcomes or say anyone is compliant.

Return JSON with one entry per rule id given, in the same order.

input.title: Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
input.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.

input.title: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Just cause evictions
input.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

input.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
input.key_value: 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy
input.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.

input.title: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Maximum rent increase
input.key_value: Lesser of 3% of current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change
input.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

input.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance
input.key_value: the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period
input.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

input.title: Housing Stability Notification Act – Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources
input.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.

input.title: Housing Stability Notification Act – City notification of Notice to Quit / Non-renewal
input.quoted_span: Landlords must use this online form to provide tenant contact information and upload a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal of Lease.

input.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) – Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
input.quoted_span: The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.

input.title: Petition for a special law authorizing Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections (H.3744)
input.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

input.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy – criminal history
input.key_value: Convictions more than 5 years old may not be considered
input.quoted_span: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on a case-by-case basis.
